summary: Accepted ADR still describes new PASS records as the five-field legacy shape
whyMissed: Worker updated normative augmentations but overlooked the repository rule to keep the relevant durable ADR aligned

summary: Validation and append are not serialized, so concurrent CLI calls can commit discipline-violating records
whyMissed: Tests invoke the CLI sequentially and never exercise concurrent writers between the ledger read and append

summary: A killed lock holder leaves a lock directory that prevents all future appends until manual cleanup
whyMissed: The concurrency remediation tested competing live processes and normal cleanup but not abnormal holder termination or recovery

summary: The persistent ledger lock file is untracked runtime state that can trip the auto-loop clean-worktree guard
whyMissed: The remediation verified kernel ownership and crash recovery but did not check the persistent lock pathname against the workflow clean-worktree contract

summary: Predictable temporary lock paths are not validated for ownership type symlinks or existing permissions
whyMissed: The remediation tested worktree cleanliness and lock lifecycle but not pre-existing temporary paths or their ownership and modes

summary: FFI library selection supports glibc Linux and macOS only and can fail during module loading elsewhere
whyMissed: Tests ran only on the current host and duplicated the same FFI selection instead of verifying platform and libc compatibility

summary: Hardlink safety does not revalidate link counts at the chmod and flock boundaries
whyMissed: The worker tested only a hardlink present before opening and did not account for link-count changes between descriptor snapshot chmod and flock

summary: Lock lifecycle tests depend on a test-only exported append API and time hook
whyMissed: Replacing Python reused internal production control flow rather than the documented CLI seam

summary: Hardlink TOCTOU remains between the final link-count check and fchmod
whyMissed: The boundary test injects before validation rather than at fchmod so it does not prove the remaining gap safe

summary: Restrictive umask can create a new lock with unusable mode that the same invocation rejects
whyMissed: Mode tests covered ordinary umask and malformed existing locks but not creation when umask masks owner permissions

summary: Native required-check policy loses GitHub App identity, allowing a same-named check or legacy status to appear to satisfy an app-bound requirement
whyMissed: Tests used unique check names and did not model app-bound native policy or identical contexts from different apps

summary: The complete annotation observation surface is filtered by required policy and current check outcome during collection
whyMissed: Tests asserted annotations only from one failed required check and omitted optional or passing-check annotations

summary: Historical changes-requested reviews are emitted as currently blocking without folding reviews into actionable latest state
whyMissed: Tests used different authors for approval and change request and did not cover a reviewer who later approved

summary: Public budget overrides allow callers to exceed the approved fixed head and transaction limits
whyMissed: Tests used only default limits and did not attempt oversized caller overrides

summary: Compact packets omit refresh references for native policy and annotation evidence
whyMissed: Tests asserted only selected refresh references and did not establish complete refresh coverage for every normalized evidence surface

summary: Single-record tagged batches, including PASS and duplicate-only Review Run Summaries, are always rejected
whyMissed: Append tests exercised only a two-record FIX batch, while single-record PASS coverage tested the schema rather than the append Interface

summary: Finding, Publication, and Recap UUIDs are checked in separate maps, allowing one event UUID to be reused across record types
whyMissed: Tests cover duplicate identities within each record type but not cross-type collisions against the documented globally unique event-identity invariant

summary: Append failures on the final candidate line omit the required JSONL line number
whyMissed: Schema tests assert line-numbered relationship errors, while append tests assert only rejection and atomicity; the CLI deliberately selects the final error's bare reason

summary: Tagged batch shape and append-discipline failures still omit their candidate JSONL line number
whyMissed: Fix-cycle regression coverage uses a metadata relationship error that reaches whole-ledger parsing but does not exercise malformed Subject SHA or append-discipline failures handled by earlier bare-error branches

summary: Batch validation checks only the accumulated ledger rather than enforcing a complete tagged submitted batch
whyMissed: Partial-batch coverage tests only a Review Run missing its declared Finding and does not exercise Publication-only, Recap-only, untagged, or mixed batches

summary: Full-ledger validation does not enforce tagged batch boundaries and accepts interleaved batches
whyMissed: Batch-completeness tests exercise the append CLI one submitted batch at a time; parser tests do not cover interleaved records from multiple tagged runs

summary: Some batch ordering and shape failures still omit the required candidate JSONL line
whyMissed: The out-of-order regression asserts only rejection and atomicity, not the diagnostic line number
